words.meaningIt: Diffuso, onnipresente, che si estende ovunque.
words.definitionEn: Spreading widely throughout an area or a group of people; existing in or present throughout every part of something.
examples: The impact of digital technology is pervasive in modern society.
There was a pervasive sense of anxiety before the exam results were announced.
words.exampleIt: L'impatto della tecnologia digitale è pervasivo nella società moderna.
words.commonMistake: Attenzione alla pronuncia /pəˈveɪsɪv/, non 'per-va-sive' all'italiana. Spesso confuso con 'invasive', che ha una connotazione più negativa e di intrusione.
words.cloze: The culture of innovation became so ____ that it permeated every department of the company.

words.meaningIt: Diverso, differente, non correlato o non confrontabile.
words.definitionEn: Essentially different in kind; not allowing comparison; containing elements very different from one another.
examples: The team comprised individuals with disparate skills and backgrounds.
We need to find common ground among these disparate viewpoints.
words.exampleIt: Il team era composto da individui con competenze e background disparati.
words.commonMistake: Spesso confuso con 'desperate' (disperato). Attenzione alla pronuncia /ˈdɪspərət/, non /ˈdɛspərət/.
words.cloze: The research project involved analyzing data from several ____ sources, each with its own methodology.

words.meaningIt: Retribuzione, compenso per servizi o lavoro, include salario, bonus, benefici.
words.definitionEn: Money paid for work or a service, typically a salary, wages, or other financial compensation, including benefits.
examples: The remuneration package for the new CEO includes a generous bonus scheme.
Employees are seeking fair remuneration for their increased workload.
words.exampleIt: Il pacchetto di retribuzione per il nuovo CEO include un generoso sistema di bonus.
words.commonMistake: Non è un falso amico, ma gli italiani tendono a usare 'salary' anche in contesti formali dove 'remuneration' sarebbe più appropriato per indicare il compenso totale, inclusi benefici e bonus.
words.cloze: The company reviews its employee ____ annually to ensure competitiveness in the market and attract top talent.

words.meaningIt: Imperativo, essenziale, di vitale importanza; qualcosa che deve essere fatto.
words.definitionEn: Of vital importance; crucial. Can also refer to an essential or urgent thing.
examples: It is imperative that we respond to customer feedback promptly.
Cost reduction has become an imperative for many businesses facing economic uncertainty.
words.exampleIt: È imperativo che rispondiamo prontamente al feedback dei clienti.
words.commonMistake: Non confonderlo con l'italiano 'imperativo' nel senso grammaticale. Qui significa 'essenziale' o 'urgente'. Attenzione alla pronuncia: lo stress è sulla seconda sillaba /ɪmˈpɛrətɪv/.
words.cloze: Ensuring data security is an absolute ____ in today's digital landscape for any responsible company.

words.meaningIt: Valutare, soppesare (pro e contro), considerare attentamente prima di decidere.
words.definitionEn: To consider carefully the good and bad aspects of something before making a decision or judgment.
examples: We need to weigh up the pros and cons before making a final decision.
She was weighing up her options after receiving two job offers.
words.exampleIt: Dobbiamo soppesare i pro e i contro prima di prendere una decisione finale.
words.commonMistake: Gli italiani potrebbero usare 'evaluate' o 'consider', ma 'weigh up' è più colloquiale e autentico per esprimere il bilanciamento di diverse parti. Non dire 'weigh up the decision', ma 'weigh up the options/pros and cons'.
words.cloze: Before accepting the promotion, he had to ____ the increased responsibility against the higher salary and benefits.
